Earnest

/UR-nist/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Earnest means showing sincere and serious intent; not joking or half-hearted.

Earnest means showing sincere and serious intent; not joking or half-hearted. The apology was so earnest that even the skeptics in the room believed him.

Worked Example

Most candidates for the volunteer coordinator role gave polished, breezy interviews. Wren's was different. She had read all five years of the shelter's annual reports and asked about a failed adoption program nobody else had noticed. When she said she wanted the job, she laid out exactly which three things she would fix in her first month, and her voice never once slipped into charm or joking. The director hired her that afternoon, telling the board she had never seen a more earnest applicant.

Wren's sincere, fully serious intent — deep preparation and plain, joke-free commitment — is what makes her earnest.

How Earnest Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

sincere

sincere: genuinely meant

wholehearted

wholehearted: fully committed

Antonyms

flippant

flippant: treating serious things jokingly

insincere

insincere: not genuinely meant

How Strong Is It? — serious → zealous → earnest

serious vs. earnest

serious vs. earnest: Serious is the plain, weaker word — a mood of the moment; earnest adds deep sincerity of intent that others can feel.

zealous vs. earnest

zealous vs. earnest: Zealous is stronger than earnest: zeal burns hot and can tip into fanaticism, while earnestness stays warm, steady, and sincere.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — earnest

Root — earnest: seriousness, vigor (Old English eornost)

Put it together

Put it together: Earnest is native English stock: Old English eornost, 'seriousness, zeal in battle,' with no Latin or Greek machinery inside it to take apart. It has traveled a thousand years nearly unchanged in form and meaning, which is fitting for a word about steadiness. There is no productive root family here — its closest relatives are its own derivatives, earnestly and earnestness.

Use the root in a new word: earnestness

Use the root in a new word: earnestness: Her earnestness disarmed the whole panel — earnestness is simply the noun form of earnest, the clearest living relative the word has.
